# Figure 3
```{r MSE, eval = FALSE, include = FALSE}
#| label: Mean Squared Error (MSE)
MSE <- function (Q_hat, Q_obs) {
   return (mean((Q_hat - Q_obs)^2))
}
```

Adjust the length of the list of $\gamma$'s
```{r Auxiliar, eval = FALSE, include = FALSE}
#| label: Auxiliar Quantities
family <- c("normal", "chisq")
gamma_list <- seq(from = 0, to = 0.025, by = 0.001) # 1 - (0.01)^(1/M)

parallel_iter <- expand.grid(
    family = family,
    q_prob = q_fig3
)
# print(nrow(parallel_iter))

N <- 10^5
```

For higher values of $N$ (as in @rue2023oracle), I have to adjust oracle_fun, because the only thing I need is to compute the squared difference between $Q_{\text{obs}}$ and $\hat{Q}$. There's no need to store anything else! I´m having problems to run what´s below because of memory requirements.

## _Oracle_ Approach
```{r Oracle Fig3, eval = FALSE, include = FALSE}
#| label: Running Oracle Fig3

# Store one MSE per combination
oracle_MSE <- matrix(0, nrow = length(parallel_iter), ncol = length(gamma_list))

# In order to use parallel, I need to use the same seed as above...
for (i in seq_len(nrow(parallel_iter))) {

    data           <- generate_data(parallel_iter$family[i], N, parallel_iter$q_prob[i])
    stream         <- data$stream
    true_quantiles <- data$quantiles

    for (j in seq_len(length(gamma_list))) {
        Oracle_quantiles <- oracle_fun(N, stream, parallel_iter$gamma[i], parallel_iter$q_prob[i])$quantiles
        results_MSE[i,j] <- MSE(Oracle_quantiles, true_quantiles)
    }

    message("Completed step ", i, "\n")
}
```

```{r Figure 3 Plots, eval = FALSE, include = FALSE}

    y = results_MSE[1, ],
    type = "l", # Line Plot
```
